prior_exposure_limitation: Wider project and earlier GPT-6 involvement cannot be erased; no prior Edea-specific ChatGPT recommendation, GrokBot advice, reconciliation, October candidate/ranking/verdict files opened before Stage A
official_legality_scope: Historical 2026-10-14 current-cycle whole-list PASS; targeted current commander/Irma/Closet/Full Throttle rules, no new complete card-by-card legality batch
identity: Five-mana Human Warlock beginning-of-own-combat targeted temporary creature theft; when a creature controlled but not owned dies, return it to its owner battlefield and draw one
natural_ceiling_hypothesis: Bracket 4 Optimized, no empirical win rates

primary_hypothesis.expected_gain: Second end-step flicker-permanent-theft path akin to Thassa for an Edea-borrowed creature, even when no sacrificial outlet is available
primary_hypothesis.strongest_counterargument: Five-mana delayed artifact overlaps four-mana indestructible Thassa, bypasses Edea dies/draw/sacrifice payoffs; Irma is cheaper and can copy owned pieces and future-combat Edea ability variants

important_rules: Both Edea and Irma choose their beginning-of-combat trigger targets before either resolves; Irma cannot target the enemy creature Edea will steal in that same trigger window
Edea's opponent-owned creature dying triggers draw and returns the actual card to its owner control if still available; ownership does not change on theft
A creature exiled/returned by Thassa or Conjurer's Closet did not die, hence no Edea death draw, but comes under our control as a new permanent beyond the temporary theft
Roaming Throne naming Human or Warlock can double both Edea own-combat and opponent-owned death triggered abilities
Full Throttle additional combats trigger Edea anew; no additional main phases between its two extra combats
A temporary theft creature still controlled at beginning of own end step can be targeted by Closet before EOT cleanup
